nutritional_priorities: Moderate calorie density to prevent obesity
Joint support supplements (Glucosamine, Chondroitin, Omega-3 fatty acids)
Limited ingredients to manage potential food allergies
Moderate fat levels (avoid overly fatty foods due to sensitivity to pancreatitis and weight gain)

puppy.notes: Bulldog puppies grow rapidly, but controlled growth is vital to prevent skeletal issues like hip dysplasia. Avoid free-feeding; follow strict portion control.

adult.notes: Adult Bulldogs are prone to weight gain due to lower activity levels. Monitor caloric intake carefully and avoid high-fat commercial foods.

senior.notes: Seniors need easily digestible proteins to maintain muscle mass without stressing kidneys, along with increased joint supplements.

feeding_tips: Use slow-feeder bowls to prevent gulping air, which worsens flatulence and bloating.
Divide daily food into at least two or three smaller meals.
Monitor treats carefully; treats should not exceed 10% of daily caloric intake.

safe_foods.name: Plain Cooked Chicken
safe_foods.benefits: High-quality, lean protein source that is easy to digest. Great for sensitive stomachs.
safe_foods.serving_instructions: Boiled or baked plain without oils, butter, spices, salt, or garlic/onions. Remove skin and bones.

safe_foods.name: Plain Cooked Turkey
safe_foods.benefits: Lean protein alternative to chicken, rich in amino acids.
safe_foods.serving_instructions: Cooked thoroughly, unseasoned, bone-free, and skinless.

safe_foods.name: White or Brown Rice
safe_foods.benefits: White rice is excellent for binding stool during bouts of mild upset stomach. Brown rice provides extra fiber for healthy adults.
safe_foods.serving_instructions: Cooked thoroughly with water only; no salt, butter, or seasonings.

safe_foods.name: Pumpkin (Pure)
safe_foods.benefits: High in soluble fiber; regulates digestion, helps with both mild diarrhea and constipation.
safe_foods.serving_instructions: Use 100% pure canned pumpkin puree (NOT pumpkin pie mix). Serve 1 to 2 tablespoons depending on dog size.

safe_foods.name: Carrots
safe_foods.benefits: Low in calories, high in beta-carotene and Vitamin A. Great for dental health when given raw as a crunchy snack.
safe_foods.serving_instructions: Wash thoroughly and cut into bite-sized pieces to prevent choking, or serve baby carrots.

safe_foods.name: Green Beans
safe_foods.benefits: Low-calorie filler rich in iron, calcium, and vitamins B6, A, and C. Excellent for overweight Bulldogs needing volume without extra calories.
safe_foods.serving_instructions: Fresh or frozen (plain, unseasoned, no added sodium/butter). Steam or serve raw in small pieces.

safe_foods.name: Sweet Potatoes
safe_foods.benefits: Rich in dietary fiber, Vitamin A, C, B6, and antioxidants. Great complex carbohydrate source.
safe_foods.serving_instructions: Peel, cook thoroughly (baked or boiled), and mash without any butter, sugar, or spices.

safe_foods.name: Blueberries
safe_foods.benefits: Packed with antioxidants, fiber, and phytochemicals that support immune health.
safe_foods.serving_instructions: Wash thoroughly and serve fresh or frozen as occasional treats.

safe_foods.name: Plain Greek Yogurt
safe_foods.benefits: Contains probiotics that support gut health and calcium for bones. Choose low-fat or fat-free.
safe_foods.serving_instructions: Ensure it is plain with NO artificial sweeteners (especially xylitol). Serve 1-2 teaspoons occasionally.

safe_foods.name: Salmon (Cooked)
safe_foods.benefits: Rich in Omega-3 fatty acids, which reduce inflammation and support skin, coat, and joint health.
safe_foods.serving_instructions: Must be fully cooked (never raw) with all bones removed. No seasonings.

toxic_foods.name: Grapes and Raisins
toxic_foods.toxic_agent: Unknown toxin causing rapid kidney failure

toxic_foods.name: Avocado
toxic_foods.toxic_agent: Persin (found in fruit, pit, leaves, and bark)

toxic_foods.name: Yeast Dough
toxic_foods.toxic_agent: Ethanol fermentation and expansion in stomach
